themes_detail.label: SPIT Inspection Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints spiked dramatically to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks (1233% increase, z-score 9.55), suggesting either a targeted enforcement operation or emerging code violations in a specific area of Bushwick that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% spike)
Z-score of 9.55 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
SPIT typically inspects for structural/life-safety violations in problem buildings
reporting_angles: Which buildings or blocks triggered SPIT enforcement this week? Is there a pattern (e.g., illegal conversions, overcrowding)?
Interview DOB to determine if this reflects a targeted sweep or reactive response to complaints

themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Infrastructure Deteriorating
themes_detail.summary: Bus Stop Shelter complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.2 per week (1100% increase, z-score 4.16), signaling rapid deterioration of transit infrastructure in a neighborhood heavily dependent on bus service.
evidence: 3 bus stop shelter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike)
Aligns with repeated community board budget request for 'new or expanded park or amenity' suggesting chronic transit/pedestrian infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Document the specific bus stops with broken/missing shelters; interview riders about safety and weather exposure
Why are repairs delayed? MTA maintenance backlog or funding constraints?

themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Reports Surge
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints jumped to 13 LAST WEEK, a 154% increase from the 5.1 weekly baseline (z-score 3.48), indicating either a localized animal welfare crisis or heightened community reporting of existing cruelty.
evidence: 13 animal abuse complaints last week vs. 5.1 weekly average (154% increase)
Z-score of 3.48 indicating statistically significant anomaly
No Reddit or local news mentions yet, suggesting emerging story before mainstream pickup
reporting_angles: What specific incidents were reported? Are they concentrated in one neighborhood/park?
Interview ASPCA or NYC animal welfare advocates about whether Bushwick has known animal cruelty hotspots or insufficient enforcement

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints surged to 9 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 243% jump from the 2.6 weekly baseline (z-score 6.43), potentially linked to mold, poor ventilation, or heating/cooling issues in residential buildings—especially relevant given 782 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days.
evidence: 9 indoor air quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average (243% spike)
782 heat/hot water complaints over 90-day period suggests systemic building maintenance issues that compound air quality problems
reporting_angles: Are these complaints concentrated in specific buildings or across the district? Do they correlate with known problem landlords?
Interview residents about specific symptoms (mold, inadequate heating, ventilation failures) and whether complaints to landlords were ignored

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Incidents Up 172%
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints jumped to 16 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 172% increase from the 5.9 weekly baseline (z-score 4.28), suggesting elevated community distress calls for disorder or minor criminal activity not captured in major crime statistics.
evidence: 16 non-emergency police complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.9 weekly average (172% increase)
No corresponding spike in major noise or parking complaints this week, suggesting distinct incident type
reporting_angles: What types of incidents are driving non-emergency calls (trespassing, loitering, disorderly conduct)?
Are 311 reports a leading indicator of neighborhood disorder? Interview NYPD 83rd Precinct about response patterns
